subject: Observability ingestion & evidence handoff for BlueWave private deployment
messages:
From: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@bluewave-sys.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Observability ingestion & evidence handoff for BlueWave private deployment

Hi team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. To move our private (VPC/on-prem) deployment into security review we need a concise mapping of what telemetry you can export from the private control plane and what we must provide from our side. Specifically: 

- Exact log types exported (application logs, audit trails, agent heartbeat, runtime metrics) and sample header lines we can validate against Splunk HEC ingestion.
- Trace hook formats and where Redwood expects trace IDs to appear (HTTP headers, gRPC metadata).
- Expected TLS mutual-auth handshake details for the forwarder, and certificate rotation cadence.
- Any on-disk artifacts Redwood will collect during an evidence request (bundles, hashed manifests).

We also need an initial evidence checklist to feed our compliance team (SOC2 readiness). Can you attach a sample checklist and a tiny sample export so our SecOps can run it through ingestion?

Priority: medium; we'd like the checklist and sample by EOD tomorrow to stay on our audit timeline.

Thanks,
Alex Barnes
Senior Security Engineer
BlueWave Systems

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@bluewave-sys.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-19T13:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability ingestion & evidence handoff for BlueWave private deployment

Alex —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a lightweight evidence checklist (bluewave-evidence-checklist.pdf) and a tiny sample of export headers (onprem-export-sample-headers.txt) from a recent VPC-onprem trial we ran. High-level answers inline below; full detail in the checklist/attachments.

1) Log types exported
- Application logs: JSON lines with timestamp, level, service, instance_id, request_id, message.
- Audit trails: immutable append-only events (user/role/action/resource/timestamp).
- Runtime metrics: Prometheus-style metrics scraped at 15s by default; we expose a short-lived scrape endpoint for the forwarder.
- Heartbeats/agent health: periodic status messages (ttl, version, pid).

2) Trace hooks
- We accept W3C traceparent headers on HTTP and the equivalent metadata on gRPC (x-traceparent).
- Default propagation: traceparent + baggage. We also support OpenTelemetry proto spans over a mTLS-encrypted collector pipeline.
- For SIEM correlation, include request_id and user_id in span attributes; our traces link to logs via request_id.

3) mTLS forwarder details
- Mutual TLS with client cert validation against customer CA; certs rotate on a 90-day cadence by default (configurable).
- TLS: TLS1.3 recommended; cipher-suite list in checklist.
- Forwarder authenticates to Redwood ingestion endpoint; we can accept connections from a customer forwarder or provide a hardened sidecar.

4) On-disk artifacts during evidence requests
- We can provide a gzipped evidence bundle containing: hashed manifest (sha256) of exported files, truncated logs for the requested window, and trace snippets. We do not collect full customer PII — manifests list redaction markers where applicable.

Next steps I propose:
- I will hand this to Kimberly and Hiro for the SIEM ingestion specifics (sample HEC payload, recommended index/metadata mapping).
- Kimberly/Hiro, can you produce a 1-page HEC mapping and a short example payload for Splunk/Elastic?
- Alex/Tim, we'll schedule a 45-minute intake to validate the sample ingestion; I put a provisional slot tomorrow 16:00 CET in the shared Drive.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bluewave-evidence-checklist.pdf (6KB), onprem-export-sample-headers.txt (1KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@bluewave-sys.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-19T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability ingestion & evidence handoff for BlueWave private deployment

Alex — Mina —

Following Mina's summary, I've attached a concise HEC/Elastic mapping and an example Splunk HEC payload. Key notes:

- Splunk HEC: we recommend a dedicated index (bluewave_redwood_private) and the following event metadata: host, source, sourcetype=redwood:privatelogs, request_id, tenant_id, trace_id. See attached example.
- Payload size: keep events < 1MB; we batch up to 100 events per call.
- Field renames: if BlueWave maps request_id differently, we support a per-tenant mapping layer in the forwarder (config flag: field_map).
- Trace correlation: include trace_id and request_id in each log event for deterministic joins in SIEM dashboards.

Example (excerpt):
"{"event": {"time": 1700000000.123, "host": "bw-app-01", "request_id": "rq_8f3b...", "trace_id": "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01", "message": "user lookup succeeded", "level": "info"}, "index": "bluewave_redwood_private" }"

I've also included a short checklist to validate that the customer's forwarder is sending the correct fields. If you'd like, Hiro can spin up a temporary ingest endpoint in our staging environment for a live test of the sample payload.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Technical Program Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: splunk-hec-sample.json (1.5KB)

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@bluewave-sys.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability ingestion & evidence handoff for BlueWave private deployment

Alex / Team —

Thanks for the patience. I stood up the temporary staging HEC endpoint and validated the sample payload Kim sent. Observations: 

- The sample ingested cleanly into index bluewave_redwood_private; timestamps preserved; trace_id fields searchable.
- We saw an edge case where very long request_id values (over 256 chars) are truncated by our default processing pipeline — config change in forwarder fixes this (field_limit_chars).
- mTLS handshake succeeded when using the test certificates you provided; cert rotation when using our sidecar requires a short restart window (~45s) for the sidecar to reload CA bundles.

I scheduled a 45-minute intake for tomorrow 15:00 CET (invitation sent to Alex/Tim). For the intake please have:
- a sample forwarder config (you can send it ahead to the Drive link)
- a small export (100-500 events) so we can exercise batching and field mappings

I'll capture the session notes in Jira BW-5421 and attach the final ingestion test log bundle to the Drive folder.

Cheers,
Hiro Tanaka
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Observability
Redwood Inference
